goodbye.note: In quick speech often khodaafez. Casual: baay (بای).

please.note: Used in requests. When offering something or inviting someone in, say befarmaayid (بفرمایید).

thank_you.note: Just as common: merci (مرسی). More formal: moteshakkeram (متشکرم).

youre_welcome.note: When thanked for something you gave: ghaabeli nadaasht (قابلی نداشت), 'it was nothing'.

sorry.note: For small things just say bebakhshid (ببخشید).

excuse_me.note: Also a quick 'sorry', e.g. when you bump into someone or squeeze past.

how_are_you.note: Also common and polite: khoob hastid? (خوب هستید؟)

im_fine.note: It's polite to ask back: shomaa chetorid? (شما چطورید؟)

whats_your_name.note: Extra polite: esm-e sharifetoon chiye? (اسم شریفتون چیه؟)

my_name_is.note: Lit. 'I am …', the usual way to introduce yourself. 'My name is Maryam' is esmam Maryame (اسمم مریمه).

speak_english.note: Lit. 'Do you know English?' Also: engelisi sohbat mikonid? (انگلیسی صحبت می‌کنید؟)

speak_slowly.note: To ask for a repeat: mishe tekraar konid? (می‌شه تکرار کنید؟)

what.note: Formal che (چه) is used inside a sentence, not alone. If you didn't catch something, bale? (بله؟) is politer.

when.note: Key rhymes with 'day'. Same letters as ki (who); the vowel mark just tells them apart and is usually left out.

who.note: Formal: che kasi (چه کسی). Same spelling as key (when); context tells them apart.

where_bathroom.note: Signs usually say servis-e behdaashti (سرویس بهداشتی).

can_you_help.note: Start with bebakhshid (ببخشید) when stopping a stranger.

one.note: Persian digit: ۱. Before a noun in speech it becomes ye (یه): ye chaay, 'one tea'.

four.note: Persian digit: ۴. In everyday speech usually chaar.

six.note: Persian digit: ۶. In Tehran speech often shish.

nine.note: Persian digit: ۹. Spelled like na (no) but said noh.

bill_please.note: Where you pay at the counter, just ask: cheghadr shod? (چقدر شد؟), 'What do I owe?'

delicious.note: Often preceded by bah bah (به‌به). To thank the cook: dastetoon dard nakone (دستتون درد نکنه).

enjoy_meal.note: Said when serving food or to someone eating. A host invites guests to start with befarmaayid (بفرمایید).

left.note: On the left: dast-e chap (دست چپ). Turn left: bepichid chap (بپیچید چپ).

right.note: On the right: dast-e raast (دست راست). Turn right: bepichid raast (بپیچید راست).

straight_ahead.note: Go straight on: mostaghim berid (مستقیم برید).

stop_here.note: Very common in taxis: haminjaa piyaade misham (همین‌جا پیاده می‌شم), 'I'll get out here'.

train_station.note: A city's main station is often just called raah-aahan (راه‌آهن), 'the railway'.

want_to_go.note: Also: mikhaam be … beram (می‌خوام به … برم). In a taxi, the place plus lotfan is enough.

one_ticket.note: Ye is spoken 'one' (written yek, یک). Belit is also spelled بلیط.

too_expensive.note: To ask for a discount: takhfif midid? (تخفیف می‌دید؟)

cheaper.note: Lit. 'Don't you have cheaper?', which is how Iranians usually ask.

id_like_this.note: Also: ino barmidaaram (اینو برمی‌دارم), 'I'll take this'.

pay_card.note: Also common: kaartkhaan daarid? (کارت‌خوان دارید؟), 'Do you have a card machine?'

cash.note: I'll pay cash: naghdi hesaab mikonam (نقدی حساب می‌کنم).

open.note: Door signs often read baaz ast (باز است), 'is open'.

closed.note: Shut for the day or a holiday: ta'til (تعطیل), also common on signs.

good_evening.note: Asr is late afternoon to early evening; after dark most people simply say salaam.

see_you_later.note: To a friend: ba'dan mibinamet (بعداً می‌بینمت). Also common: fe'lan (فعلاً), 'bye for now'.

wait_moment.note: Short and very common: ye lahze (یه لحظه).

need_doctor.note: More casual: doktor laazem daaram (دکتر لازم دارم).

im_lost.note: Also: raahamo gom kardam (راهمو گم کردم), 'I've lost my way'.

lost_phone.note: Gooshi (گوشی) is the everyday word for a mobile phone.

be_careful.note: To one friend: movaazeb baash! (مواظب باش!)

no_problem.note: Also very common: eshkaal nadaare (اشکال نداره), 'it's okay'.

i_like_it.note: On first seeing or tasting it: khosham oomad (خوشم اومد).

welcome.note: Written and on signs: khosh aamadid (خوش آمدید).

congratulations.note: For a birthday, wedding or new purchase: mobaarak baashe! (مبارک باشه!)

my_family.note: In speech often khaanevaadam. Also: khaanevaade-ye man (خانواده‌ی من).

mother.note: Mum: maamaan (مامان), what most people call their own mother.

brother.note: Informal: daadaash (داداش), also used affectionately for a male friend.

sister.note: The و is silent. Informal: aabji (آبجی).

child.note: Means both 'kid' and 'son or daughter'. Formal: farzand (فرزند).

friend.note: Same for a male or female friend. Casual, for a close mate: rafigh (رفیق).

this_is_my_friend.note: Same for a female friend. More formal: ishoon doost-e man hastan (ایشون دوست من هستن).

monday.note: The week starts on Saturday (shanbe) and days count on from it: do-shanbe, 'two-shanbe'.

friday.note: The main weekly day off in Iran.

saturday.note: The first day of the Iranian week.

what_day.note: Lit. 'How-many-shanbe is today?', the usual way to ask the weekday.

next_week.note: Also very common: hafte-ye dige (هفته‌ی دیگه).

fifteen.note: Persian digits: ۱۵. In speech usually poonzdah.

hundred.note: Persian digits: ۱۰۰. No 'one' needed: sad on its own is a hundred.

thousand.note: Persian digits: ۱۰۰۰. As with sad, no 'one' is needed.

how_old.note: Also: chand saal daarid? (چند سال دارید؟)

years_old.note: More formal: … saal daaram (… سال دارم).

black.note: For clothes, cars and hair people often say meshki (مشکی).

this_one.note: To ask for it: ino mikhaam (اینو می‌خوام), 'I want this'.

that_one.note: Oon is the spoken form of aan (آن), 'that'.

another_one.note: Dige is the spoken form of digar (دیگر), 'other'.

its_hot.note: Lit. 'the air is warm'. I'm hot: garmame (گرممه).

its_windy.note: Lit. 'wind is coming', like rain. Stormy: havaa toofaaniye (هوا طوفانیه).

beautiful_day.note: Lit. 'What nice weather!', the usual way to say it. Also: che rooz-e ghashangi! (چه روز قشنگی!)

have_reservation.note: Also: ye otaagh rezerv kardam (یه اتاق رزرو کردم), 'I booked a room'.

room.note: Single room: otaagh-e yek-nafare (اتاق یک‌نفره); double: do-nafare (دونفره).

passport.note: Official word, on forms and signs: gozarnaame (گذرنامه).

luggage.note: Strictly 'suitcase'; in speech chamedoon. Checked bags at the airport: baar (بار).

wifi_password.note: Many say pasvord (پسورد) instead of ramz.

check_out_time.text: ساعت چند باید اتاق رو تحویل بدم؟
check_out_time.roman: saa'at chand baayad otaagh ro tahvil bedam?
check_out_time.note: Lit. 'What time must I hand the room back?' Check-out time: saa'at-e takhliye (ساعت تخلیه).

next_train.note: Also: ghataar-e ba'di saa'at chande? (قطار بعدی ساعت چنده؟)

i_work_in.note: E.g. too baank kaar mikonam, 'I work in a bank'. Written: dar (در) instead of too.

im_student.note: Same for men and women. A school pupil: daanesh-aamooz (دانش‌آموز).

office.note: Also means 'notebook'. A government office: edaare (اداره).

meeting.note: I have a meeting: jalase daaram (جلسه دارم).

im_busy.note: Lit. 'my head is crowded'. Also: kaar daaram (کار دارم), 'I have things to do'.

day_off.note: It's my day off: emrooz ta'tilam (امروز تعطیلم). Leave from work: morakhasi (مرخصی).

colleague.note: Same word for men and women.

good_job.note: To a colleague or boss, kheyli aali bood! (خیلی عالی بود!) sounds less like a teacher.

table_for_two.text: یه میز برای دو نفر، لطفاً
table_for_two.roman: ye miz baraa-ye do nafar, lotfan
table_for_two.note: Also: ye miz-e do-nafare mikhaastam (یه میز دونفره می‌خواستم).

vegetarian_food.note: Do you have any?: ghazaa-ye giyaahi daarid? (غذای گیاهی دارید؟)

more_water.text: لطفاً یه کم دیگه آب بیارید
more_water.roman: lotfan ye kam dige aab biyaarid

no_sugar.note: Tea usually comes with sugar cubes, ghand (قند), on the side.

im_full.note: Hosts often insist on more; a polite no: na merci, sir shodam (نه مرسی، سیر شدم).

takeaway.note: If asked injaa meyl mikonid? (اینجا میل می‌کنید؟), just say mibaram (می‌برم).

it_was_delicious.note: To a host or cook, add dastetoon dard nakone (دستتون درد نکنه).

stomach.note: Stomach ache is usually delam dard mikone (دلم درد می‌کنه). The organ: me'de (معده).

head_hurts.note: Also: sardard daaram (سردرد دارم), 'I have a headache'.

call_ambulance.note: Also: zang bezanid orzhaans! (زنگ بزنید اورژانس!). The emergency number is 115 (۱۱۵).

get_well.note: Very common: ishaallaa zoodtar khoob mishid (ایشالا زودتر خوب می‌شید).

lets_meet.note: To set a time: ye gharaar bezaarim (یه قرار بذاریم).

are_you_free.note: Also: fardaa vaghtetoon aazaade? (فردا وقتتون آزاده؟)

call_me.note: To a friend: behem zang bezan (بهم زنگ بزن).

your_number.note: Lit. 'How much is your number?', the usual way to ask.

see_you_soon.note: Lit. 'in hope of meeting'. Casual: mibinamet! (می‌بینمت!)

have_nice_day.note: Shorter: rooz khosh! (روز خوش!) Before an outing: khosh begzare! (خوش بگذره!)

good_luck.note: To a friend: movaffagh baashi! (موفق باشی!)

thanks_a_lot.note: Also: kheyli merci (خیلی مرسی). For a favour or a meal: dastetoon dard nakone (دستتون درد نکنه).

miss_you.note: Lit. 'my heart has got tight for you'. To an elder: delam baraatoon tang shode (دلم براتون تنگ شده).
